title: ELMA: Benchmarking Anaphoric Compositions for Long-Term Text-to-Motion Generation
claim: Input instructions grow in difficulty from independent atomic steps, to simultaneous actions, to segments that depend on earlier ones.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, stacked bottom-to-top boxes with dependency arrows in last panel
description: Three side-by-side panels, labeled (a), (b), (c), each a stack of three rounded light-blue boxes. Each stack is read bottom to top, along a time axis. A dashed diagonal line separates the panels, and a bold arrow labeled 'Time' sits at the right. Panel (a) shows single-word actions: Run, Walk, Sit. Panel (b) has boxes with a pink lower region for a second concurrent action: 'Walk and waving' and 'Walk and carrying a box'. Panel (c) has natural-language segments with red text on yellow highlights: 'his right hand', 'holding it', 'Put it down'. Curved black arrows link these phrases across boxes to show the dependencies. The eye goes first to the red-on-yellow highlights and arrows in (c).
caption: Three types of text composition in long-term motion generation: As shown in (a), atomic composition is the simplest input format, where a sequence is constructed from consecutive segments that each represent a single action. The concurrent composition illustrated in (b) is a more complex format than (a), as individual segments may contain two or more actions. Finally, the anaphoric composition depicted in (c) is an even more complex format, characterized by cross-dependencies across the input segments.
abstract: Text-guided long-term human motion generation is essential for applications such as continuously operating digital avatars. Despite recent progress on short clips, existing models struggle with multi-segment instructions that involve anaphora, where constraints established in earlier segments must be preserved over time. In this paper, we introduce a novel task of long-term motion generation from such anaphoric compositions. To address this gap, we present ELMA, an episodic long-term motion dataset with dense segment-level annotations that preserve cross-segment dependencies. Built via a fully automated collection and filtering pipeline, ELMA extracts high-quality, continuous 30-second clips from in-the-wild videos, capturing the episodic narratives necessary for long-range state modeling. Using ELMA, we benchmark representative long-term motion generation models under independent and anaphoric instruction settings, and study whether contextual fine-tuning improves long-range state modeling. Our extensive experiments provide insights into the capabilities and limitations of existing models in handling context-dependent instructions. These findings highlight the challenge of modeling cross-segment dependencies and offer valuable directions for developing more coherent and semantically consistent long-term motion generation models.
